dedupe_keys.name: nist tennessee eastman simulation code for industrial wireless performance evaluation tesim

description: This NIST software release contains the Tennessee Eastman chemical process model packaged for hardware-based simulation within the NIST Industrial Wireless project. The Tennessee Eastman process is a standard benchmark plant with reactors, separators and recycle loops used in control and fault studies. NIST optimised the code for integration with external sensor and actuator equipment, so that the generic process, not tied to any real site, runs in real time while its measurements and control signals travel over real or emulated wireless links, and the operational performance of the plant can be evaluated under different wireless scenarios, including cyber-security conditions. It was released by Richard Candell (updated 4 November 2016, issued 2017) under the NIST open licence and is hosted in the usnistgov tesim repository on GitHub, which could not be opened from this session. Caveats: it is a benchmark process, not a real plant, it is tailored to NIST's test set-up, and the repository contents and last update were not read here. For simulation it couples a chemical plant model to a communications network, so it can show how packet loss, latency or attacks on plant networks degrade process control, a building block for cyber-physical interdependency studies. Related catalogue records include the Tennessee Eastman process anomaly detection data and the NIST smart manufacturing systems test bed.
